articles.title: I Built a Free Python Error Fixer (No Login Required)
articles.excerpt: Debugging Python errors can be a frustrating cycle. You copy a 20-line traceback, paste it into ChatGPT, and hope you didn't hit your message limit for the day. I wanted a faster, frictionless way to…
articles.body: Debugging Python errors can be a frustrating cycle. You copy a 20-line traceback, paste it into ChatGPT, and hope you didn't hit your message limit for the day. I wanted a faster, frictionless way to fix errors without the "subscribe to continue" popups. So, I built a Free Python Error Fixer that requires absolutely zero login. What does it do? You paste your Python traceback, and it gives you: The corrected code block. A brief explanation of why the error happened (e.g., TypeErrors, ImportErrors). 👉 Try it here: xoneai.in/tools/python-error-fixer How I Built It (Tech Stack) I wanted this tool to be blazing fast, so here is the stack behind it: Frontend: React + Vite + Tailwind CSS (super lightweight). Backend: FastAPI (Python). AI Engine: Groq API for near-instant generation.
articles.author: Monika Pareek

articles.title: Anthropic FlashProve proves which model answered with a zkSNARK proof
articles.excerpt: 📅 November 3, 2026 • TechCrunch / Anthropic Anthropic published a cryptographic answer to a question users normally cannot check: did the claimed model actually produce this response? In a research p…
articles.body: 📅 November 3, 2026 • TechCrunch / Anthropic Anthropic published a cryptographic answer to a question users normally cannot check: did the claimed model actually produce this response? In a research post titled “Progress on provable inference for large language models”, the company introduces FlashProve — a zkSNARK-based proof that an answer was generated by exactly the stated model, without revealing the weights. zkSNARKs are a cryptographic technique that lets one party prove a statement is true while keeping the underlying data hidden — here, that a specific generation came from specific weights that stay sealed. Per Anthropic, the proof travels with the response, so a user or an auditor can verify the origin of an output independently of the provider's assurances.

articles.title: Why Stakeholder Management is an Agile Team Sport, Not Just a Product Owner Duty
articles.excerpt: You have likely seen it happen. A development team sits in relative isolation, quietly grinding through Jira tickets. Meanwhile, the Product Owner runs frantically from meeting to meeting, absorbing b…
articles.body: You have likely seen it happen. A development team sits in relative isolation, quietly grinding through Jira tickets. Meanwhile, the Product Owner runs frantically from meeting to meeting, absorbing business requirements, filtering them, and passing them down to the team. This is the proxy wall. It is one of the most common, deeply embedded anti-patterns in modern software delivery. Treating stakeholder management as a solo sport exclusively for the Product Owner guarantees missed context, delayed feedback loops, and ultimately, mediocre technical solutions. Your entire Agile team needs direct, structured exposure to stakeholders. Let us break down exactly why, and how to fix this delivery bottleneck. What Happens When the Product Owner Becomes a Proxy Wall?

articles.title: “Available” Is Not Booked: A Race-Safe Contract for AI Property Viewings
articles.excerpt: “Available” Is Not Booked: A Race-Safe Contract for AI Property Viewings A voice agent can identify a property, understand a caller, read a calendar, and still create a bad appointment. The dangerous…
articles.body: “Available” Is Not Booked: A Race-Safe Contract for AI Property Viewings A voice agent can identify a property, understand a caller, read a calendar, and still create a bad appointment. The dangerous gap is between “the slot looked free” and “the booking system committed it.” If two calls cross that gap, both callers can hear a confident confirmation while only one viewing can happen. The decision rule is simple: say “confirmed” only after the system that owns the viewing has durably accepted one specific booking, under a conflict rule that also applies to concurrent requests. Our real-estate agency overview describes the voice-agent use case; this guide adds the operational contract a buyer should demand before letting an agent confirm viewings.

articles.body: Every developer has a database horror story. Mine usually starts with a terminal, a production connection string, and the words "quick fix". So I built DBAdminer : a database explorer that starts in read-only mode , because it assumes you're tired, caffeinated, and one typo away from a postmortem. What is it? A database explorer for Go . Point it at PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, or SQLite, open your browser, and poke around: tables, data, a SQL console, the works. Full access is there when you want it, but you have to ask for it. articles.body: Ahead of the release of Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI , Nintendo is launching its own fall juggernaut: a Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . The remake, which is releasing 28 years after the launch of the original version on Nintendo 64, has a much more realistic visual style and some modern improvements like a jump button, a way to sprint, full voice acting, and a “Threads of Time” feature that helps you keep track of your progress. But while the game has a new coat of paint, it appears many elements will still remain faithful to the classic N64 release. Nintendo has also launched a special version of the Switch 2 and Switch 2 Pro Controller with Triforce imagery to celebrate the game.

articles.excerpt: The Hubble Space Telescope is healthy but is being pulled down toward Earth by atmospheric drag. NASA is considering options to extend the iconic telescope's work.
articles.body: NASA is reviving discussions to rescue the Hubble Space Telescope, which is operating well but is on track to reenter Earth's atmosphere about six years from now. The agency issued a request for information (RFI) on Oct. 29 for "in-space servicing" capabilities, which could include boosting Hubble's orbit (which is naturally degrading due to atmospheric drag), or even a mission to "enhance its capabilities" in some way. Hubble, which launched in April 1990 in partnership with the European Space Agency , was serviced five times by astronauts on space shuttle missions, the most recent being in 2009.

articles.body: New research suggests that collisions between stars in the early universe were common, which could help explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The team behind this research performed simulations of the early universe and found stellar systems were densely packed, leading to stars frequently slamming into each other. While rapid collisions would have destroyed the stars involved, slower collisions would have led to repeated mergers, creating single over-massive stars, which could collapse and form larger-than-usual black holes at the end of their lives. These could be the seeds of the first supermassive black holes.

articles.title: Dimorphos in sight: Europe's Hera probe gets its 1st look at battered space rock (photo)
articles.excerpt: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart.
articles.body: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart. Hera is nearing the end of its voyage to the Didymos asteroid system, having launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in October 2024. The spacecraft snapped the image of Didymos and the smaller Dimorphos on Oct. 18 from a distance of 795 miles (1280 kilometers) from the pair, which are currently about 122 million miles (197 million km) from Earth. "With this image, the smaller Dimorphos asteroid becomes visible for the first time," Michael Kueppers, Hera project scientist at the European Space Agency (ESA), said in a statement .
